title: Maximize Area of Square Hole in Grid
summary: Given integers n and m, and two arrays hBars and vBars, determine the largest possible area of a square hole in a grid with n+2 horizontal and m+2 vertical bars.
statement: Given integers n and m, and two arrays hBars and vBars, determine the largest possible area of a square hole in a grid with n+2 horizontal and m+2 vertical bars. Bars are indexed starting at 1, and some can be removed from hBars and vBars to maximize the square hole area.
constraints: The grid has n+2 horizontal and m+2 vertical bars; removable interior bar indices are distinct.
Removing r consecutive bars creates a span of r+1 cells in that direction.
Return the maximum square area obtainable by removing listed bars.
hints: A square side is limited by consecutive removable bars in both directions.
Sort each bar list and find its longest consecutive run, then add one for cell span.
Take the smaller horizontal/vertical span and square it.
Only consecutive removed separators merge adjacent unit cells, and a square must fit in both independent directions, proving the minimum-span bound is attainable.
editorial: Only consecutive removed separators merge adjacent unit cells, and a square must fit in both independent directions, proving the minimum-span bound is attainable.

tests.explanation: Two consecutive horizontal removals allow height three, but the vertical span limits the square side to two.
Removing one bar in each direction creates a two-by-two square of area four.
